sources.title: Korea Heritage Service / Royal Palaces and Tombs Center — Gyeongbokgung Palace and Its History
sources.studied: Official descriptive text and historical overview, not copied photographs, sprites or game maps
sources.observed: Primary Joseon palace, wide Yukjo Street before the main Gwanghwamun gate, and named gates in several directions.
sources.designTranslation: A straight civic approach, large south gate and defined palace boundary with service gates.
sources.notClaimed: Not the real Gyeongbokgung plan, scale, current restoration or palace program.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Changdeokgung Palace Complex
sources.studied: Official descriptive text and historical overview, not copied photographs, sprites or game maps
sources.observed: Formal/residential court hierarchy within an architectural complex adapted to uneven terrain; terraces, pools and pavilions form part of the garden.
sources.designTranslation: A legible inner gate/court relationship, secondary paths that follow landscape and an open pavilion framing the pond.
sources.notClaimed: No copied Secret Garden, palace footprint, three-court reconstruction or claimed topographic survey.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies
sources.studied: Official descriptive text and historical overview, not copied photographs, sprites or game maps
sources.observed: Teaching, scholar veneration and engagement with nature are reflected in spatial organization; pavilion buildings mediate between learning and landscape.
sources.designTranslation: A quiet teaching court, separate study/library wings and a garden-facing rest place.
sources.notClaimed: Not a named historic academy or a claim that this fictional Hangul school is a historic seowon.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Historic Villages of Korea: Hahoe and Yangdong
sources.studied: Official descriptive text and historical overview, not copied photographs, sprites or game maps
sources.observed: Joseon-era villages relate houses, study halls and pavilions to forested slopes, river and fields; varied household groups participate in the settlement structure.
sources.designTranslation: Different U/L/detached residential compounds, plots and alleys responding to courts, household service yards and water.
sources.notClaimed: Not a Bukchon/Hahoe/Yangdong map or a historical shop reconstruction. Bookshop/tea/craft uses are original fictional game programs adapted to this architectural grammar.
